sections.text: Introduction

The digital 
transformer protection scheme RET 316*4 is one of the new generation of fully 
digital protection systems. It's designed for fast selective protection of two 
and three winding power transformers.

The unit detects the following faults on power 
transformers:
 - All phase faults.
 - Earth faults where the power transformer star-point 
is solidly or low-impedance grounded.
 - Inter - turn faults

This procedure
details the steps required to completely check the proper operation and
calibration of the relay. It is recommended this procedure be carried out on an
annually bases. The document is formatted the way to minimize the possibility
of error causing personal injury or damage to equipment.

The
first draft initiated by eng. Samah Mokhtar Mostafa, tested at 4 Dec. 2002 by eng. Yousef Melad Shahat, and approved by eng. Fawzy Moursy Mohamed: 
Head Sector of Aswan Network, Upper Egypt zone.
Safety Precautions

A work permit
must be issued and the qualified maintenance staff should carry the suitable
safety category,
Safety fence with caution marks surrounding the work area,
Line isolation and work permit required

Make sure that 
CT secondary circuits are shorted before isolating the current circuits for test 
distance protection

sections.text: Differential Protection test

items:
Be sure that the DC power of the relay is correct by applying a DC voltmeter 
 across points H2 and H3 on the rear of the relay
Connect AC power to the test set
Connect the current by selecting the operation of current (I) on the test set
To test winding (1):

Connect the current test lead on the current terminals of the relay T1 and T2 
 (phase R to Neutral)

Increase the value of current slowly until the relay operates and the LED of 
 (diff. protection trip) lights

Connect the current test lead on the current terminals of the relay T3 and T4 
 (phase S to Neutral)
Repeat step 6

Connect the current test lead on the current terminals of the relay T5 and T6 
 (phase T to Neutral)
Repeat step 6
To test winding (2):

Connect the current test lead on the current terminals of the relay T7 and T8 
 (phase R to Neutral)

Increase the value of current slowly until the relay operates and the LED of 
 (diff. protection trip) lights

Connect the current test lead on the current terminals of the relay T9 and T10 
 (phase S to Neutral)
Repeat step6

Connect the current test lead on the current terminals of the relay T11 and 
 T12 (phase T to Neutral)
Repeat step 6
To test winding (3)

Connect the current test lead on the current terminals of the relay T13 and 
 T14 (phase R to Neutral)

Increase the value of current slowly until the relay operates and the LED of 
 (diff. protection trip) lights

Connect the current test lead on the current terminals of the relay T15 and 
 T16 (phase S to Neutral)
Repeat step 6

Connect the current test lead on the current terminals of the relay T17 and 
 T18 (Phase T to Neutral
Repeat step 6

of external

Return relay 
and 
associated equipment to 
service

items:
Return relay to service by removing the test leads from the relay terminals 
 and the test set
Make sure CT and V T secondary circuits are in normal condition
Remove the disturbance alarm LED's on the relay which is caused by the test
Request feeder to be returned in service

Measures the currents and voltages in the secondaries of the main CT's and 
 VT's and compare the results with the values displayed by the MMC

Take phasor readings of all A C currents and voltages and compare them to 
 those for normal load condition

Check that these reading agree with station meters (MW, Mvar, Amperes and power 
 factor)
Place a copy of the test result in the field maintenance file
